note: PACK-003 build deterministic tar: a tar header carries a great deal of host state, and src/package/tar.zig takes all of it from the declaration - declared per-entry mode (so nothing becomes executable by accident), declared mtime defaulting to the epoch rather than the file's own time, zero uid/gid and a fixed uname/gname so an archive does not record which human built it, POSIX ustar magic, and names longer than a ustar field refused rather than silently split. Executable files, directories, and symbolic links are all covered; a declared mode change changes the bytes, which is what makes the policy meaningful rather than decorative. Running it found a real defect in the link check: traversal was judged from the archive root, so a legitimate ../bin/jckg from a link inside a/ was refused - the depth is now the link's own directory depth, and the escaping shapes (leading slash, and a target that climbs past the root) are asserted refusals. Fault proof: accepting any link target makes the escaping-link assertion fail (exit 1); revert byte-identical against a backup, no FAULT markers remain.
